title: Validation of the Diet Quality Screener (DQScreen) based on the Food-Based Dietary Guidelines for Germany: Evaluation of criterion validity, relative validity, and test-retest reliability
summary:
A dietetic intervention in the context of dietetic counselling/therapy must be based on valid data on the clients' eating habits. Evidence-based, standardised screeners are well suited for data collection, as they are particularly resource-efficient due to their limited length and the simultaneous collection and assessment of data. The prevention and therapy of diet-related diseases focuses on food-based dietary guidelines that aim to improve diet quality.
The aim is therefore to validate the newly developed diet quality screener (DQScreen) based on the national Food Based Dietary Guidelines (FBDG) for Germany for use in dietetic counselling and therapy.
The validation study follows a cross-over design. At t1, study participants will perform a 3-day weighted food record, collect a 24-hour urine and provide a fasting blood sample as reference methods. The DQScreen will be performed both before and after the collection of the reference methods and repeated again at t2 after a washout period of 14 days. In addition, at t1 anthropometric data and body composition are determined, socio-demographic data are collected, the physical activity of the participants is recorded and the health status of the participants is examined.

Web-DQScreen extension: Following the initial results of this study, which demonstrated the validity of the Web-DQScreen, the study will be expanded to include a further component. This will involve comparing the DQScreen, which was administered via interview during the validation study, with an adapted self-completion version (the Web-DQScreen).
conditions: diet quality screener (DQScreen) validity and reliability

interventions.name:
Evaluation of the newly developed DQScreen against biomarkers in blood and urine (criterion validity) and 3-day weighted food records (relative validity), repeated administration of the DQScreen (test-retest reliability).

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
- BMI: 18.5-34.9 kg/m2
- good written and spoken German
- Voluntary agreement to participate in the study and understanding of the study
- Availability during the study periods
- omnivorous, flexitarian or ovo-lacto vegetarian diets
- Stable body weight (< 3 kg weight gain/loss in the past 3 months)
Exclusion criteria:
- pregnant or breastfeeding women
- degree/training in food and nutritional sciences and/or dietetics
- special diets
- vegan diet
- eating disorders
- diseases that affect memory
- chronic diseases treated with medication: all forms of diabetes mellitus, heart failure, chronic kidney disease, hypertension, dyslipoproteinaemia, hyperuricaemia/gout, chronic inflammatory bowel diseases
- long-term medication with regard to the above-mentioned illnesses
- mental illnesses incl. intake of antidepressants
- weight reduction diet/weight changes
- alcoholism, drugs as of common practice (Toft et al. 2008)
- taking supplements that affect the urine/blood concentrations of biomarkers: fatty acid supplements, supplements containing antioxidants, supplements containing potassium
- electronic implants, prostheses, life-sustaining electronic systems, portable electronic medical systems (limitations of bioimpedance analysis (BIA))
- other exclusion criteria at the investigator's discretion
